The capability architecture

Talents Guiding Abilities

A buddy leans on the abilities its talents improve

Mindsplanned; this page is the plan, and the per-class table is built once the owner approves it

The owner, 2026-10-15: "would it be possible to cause buddy-bots to be more likely to use the abilities that are mentioned or affected by the spec talents they are slotted? Just... in general." And 2026-10-29: "We could use the embedding of the icon and the name and the text to maybe also guide it a little bit ... we should check token-by-token to find word-by-word relationship associations. And then maybe prioritize or increase in value the relationships that are a little unseen, like "all of your subtlety spells" or "weapon attacks" and similar."

Today

A buddy fights by the bot module's fixed priorities for its class. A talent that makes Rejuvenation stronger changes nothing about how often Rejuvenation is cast. Nothing in this plan is built yet.

Reading a talent four ways

Each talent, and each item set bonus, is read four ways, and the readings are checked against each other:

  1. The game's own list. Every class spell carries a hidden set of flags, and a talent names the flags of the spells it changes. The server applies talents by exactly this, so it is the answer that wins any disagreement.
  2. The broad targets. Some talents name no spell but a whole school of magic, a weapon kind, or a kind of ability: those are expanded to every ability of the class that matches.
  3. The icon. A talent usually wears its main ability's picture.
  4. The words, token by token, with a text embedding as a fuzzy check.

The icon

Checked in the game's spell table: Improved Rejuvenation and Rejuvenation share icon 64. Starlight Wrath shares Wrath's icon (263) but also speeds Starfire, which the icon alone misses. So the icon finds a talent's main ability, not all of them.

The words

A tooltip is read word by word. An ability's name in it ("your Rejuvenation spell") ties the two. Category phrases ("weapon attacks", "finishing moves", "Shadow spells", "bleed", a tree's name) are looked up in a small table that says which abilities each covers. A text embedding (each text turned into a list of numbers, close lists meaning close meanings) compares the talent's text with each ability's text, to catch what the table lacks. A link only the words find is shown for a look by eye before it counts.

The broad ones count for more

A talent that touches many abilities would spread thin and count for little on each. Its weight on each ability it covers is raised instead, so a buddy with talents for "all your Shadow spells" leans toward its Shadow spells as a whole. (Counting how many talents name an ability was dropped on 2026-10-22: it would make a druid cast only Healing Touch.)

At the action bar

The result is a weight for each ability: the more talent points spent in talents that touch it, the more it is favoured when the buddy chooses what to do. Abilities its talents never mention keep their ordinary weight, and an ability it does not know is never asked for (seen 2026-10-15: a hunter asked 41,000 times for an aura it did not have). The same weights steer its gems, gear and loot.

What is built once approved

A generated table for every class, read from the game's own spell tables: each talent, the abilities it touches by each reading, coloured by where the readings agree, the word-only links set apart for judging.
